extracted.intended_audience: immigration applicants, sponsors, obligors, attorneys, benefit-granting agencies, advocacy groups, and other stakeholders (commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: DHS proposed rule defining how USCIS determines inadmissibility on public charge grounds, including definitions, types and thresholds of public benefits to be considered, evidentiary requirements, factors to weigh in the totality of the circumstances, public charge bond procedures, and related procedural/filing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of public charge inadmissibility (8 CFR 212.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies the categories of aliens that are subject to the public charge inadmissibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which applicants (applicants for admission, extension of stay, change of status, adjustment of status) are subject to the public charge determination and notes exemptions where section 212(a)(4) does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (8 CFR 212.21) — key terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes key regulatory definitions, including 'public charge', 'public benefit', 'likely at any time to become a public charge', and 'household'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the universe of concepts used throughout the rule; see subsections for types of public benefits and related definitional detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge determination (8 CFR 212.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluating the likelihood of becoming a public charge is a prospective determination based on the totality of the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides details on considering the statute's mandatory factors, weighting positive and negative factors, and making a prospective (future-looking) determination rather than a retrospective one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions and waivers (8 CFR 212.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists statutory and regulatory exemptions from and waivers of inadmissibility based on public charge grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies categories of aliens and situations where public charge determinations do not apply or may be waived; affects who must demonstrate non-receipt/likelihood standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation of monetizable benefits (8 CFR 212.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology for calculating the annual aggregate amount of the portion attributable to the alien for monetizable public benefits considered in the public charge determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how DHS will apportion benefits (e.g., where a benefit covers multiple persons) and compute annual dollar values to compare to thresholds (e.g., % of FPG).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetizable public benefits — program list
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies which programs are considered 'monetizable' public benefits (e.g., SSI, TANF, General Assistance cash benefits, SNAP, certain housing programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists program-level items that count as monetizable benefits and will be valued under the valuation methodology; guidance includes examples like Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers and Section 8 Project-Based Rental Assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-monetizable public benefits — program list
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies which programs are considered 'non-monetizable' public benefits (e.g., Medicaid, institutionalization for long-term care, Medicare Part D premium/cost-sharing subsidies, subsidized public housing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes program descriptions and notes exceptions (e.g., exceptions for certain Medicaid services or for foreign-born children of U.S. citizens). Non-monetizable benefits are considered under a duration/usage standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fifteen Percent of Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG) standard for monetizable benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes to consider an alien's receipt of monetizable public benefits when such receipt is above a threshold of 15 percent of the Federal Poverty Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt above the applicable dollar threshold (15% of FPG) triggers consideration in the public charge determination; DHS provides valuation rules to compute this amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelve-Month Standard for non-monetizable benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes a 12-month duration standard for considering receipt of non-monetizable public benefits in public charge determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an alien has received one or more non-monetizable benefits for a cumulative 12 months (with DHS-defined counting rules), this may be considered in the public charge determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination rule — monetizable below 15% FPG plus non-monetizable benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes to consider combinations where monetizable benefits below the 15% FPG threshold combined with one or more non-monetizable benefits may warrant consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an approach for evaluating aggregate receipt across benefit types rather than treating program categories in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primarily dependent standard and its limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the 'primarily dependent' standard and DHS's view of its limitations for public charge determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why simplistic reliance on a 'primarily dependent' test is insufficient and how DHS will instead use specified thresholds and totality of circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Household definition in public charge context
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'household' for purposes of attributing benefits and determining public charge status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compares household definitions across benefit programs and immigration contexts and explains how DHS will treat household composition when apportioning benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective determination based on totality of circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The public charge inquiry is prospective and must weigh multiple factors in the totality of an alien's circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates evaluation of statutory factors (age, health, family status, assets/resources/financial status, education/skills, prospective immigration status and expected period of admission, affidavit of support) together rather than individually in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age as a mandatory factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Age is a factor DHS will consider when evaluating likelihood of becoming a public charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will assess whether age (e.g., very young or elderly) affects self-sufficiency and likelihood of future benefit receipt; evidentiary expectations may be described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health as a mandatory factor (including evidentiary requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Health of the applicant is a factor, with USCIS evidentiary requirements and consideration of effects for aliens with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details include medical exam evidence (Form I-693), potential exceptions, and analysis of how disabilities may affect employability or medical costs; DHS discusses evidentiary thresholds and potential accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family status as a mandatory factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Family status (household composition, dependents, marital status) is a factor in public charge assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will consider how family ties, dependents, and household composition affect financial need and access to sponsor resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assets, resources, and financial status (evidence and indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will consider assets, resources, and financial status, including specified types of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates evidence DHS may require or consider: documentation of assets/resources, evidence of financial status, records of public benefits, fee waiver records, credit reports and scores, and demonstrated financial means to pay for medical costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and skills (USCIS evidentiary requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Education and skills of the alien are factors; USCIS may require evidence to demonstrate education, training, and employability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will evaluate how education level, vocational skills, language proficiency, and certifications relate to likelihood of self-sufficiency; the rule outlines expected evidentiary submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective immigration status and expected period of admission
rubrics_metrics.description: The immigration status the alien seeks and the expected length of authorized stay are factors in the public charge determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will weigh the prospective status (e.g., temporary nonimmigrant vs. immigrant) and how long the alien is expected to remain in the U.S. when assessing future reliance on benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Support (general consideration and proposed changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of sponsorship and affidavits of support in the public charge determination; DHS proposes to consider required affidavits of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses the role of Forms I-864 series, how sponsorship commitments will be weighed, and the interplay between affidavits and other factors; also notes proposal to eliminate Form I-864W and changes in how exemptions are claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavily weighed negative factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated factors that DHS proposes to give heavy negative weight in public charge determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes lack of employability; current receipt of one or more public benefits; receipt of public benefits within the last 36 months of filing; lack of financial means to pay for medical costs; and prior findings of inadmissibility or deportability on public charge grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavily weighed positive factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated factors that DHS proposes to give heavy positive weight in public charge determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes previously excluded benefits and other strong indicia of self-sufficiency (specific examples and weighting guidance appear in the rule's factor discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of review of factors in the totality of the circumstances (favorable/unfavorable determinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework for synthesizing factors into an overall favorable or unfavorable public charge determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how DHS will conclude admissibility or inadmissibility after weighing all factors and how certain combinations of factors may lead to determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to post and requirements for Public Charge Bonds (8 CFR 213.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS's discretionary authority to accept public charge bonds for adjustment of status applicants, including bond amount, submission, substitution, cancellation, breach conditions, and appeal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies procedural rules for posting bonds (Form I-945), fee/processing rules (8 CFR 103.7), minimum bond amounts, substitution of bonds, conditions for cancellation (e.g., naturalization, permanent departure, 5-year LPR anniversary), burden of proof for cancellation (preponderance of evidence), and consequences of breach (demand, appeal rights for obligor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Breach of public charge bond — conditions and adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which a public charge bond is breached and the process for adjudication, notification, appeal, and demand for payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bond breached if alien receives public benefits defined in 8 CFR 212.21(b) after adjustment and before cancellation (with specified exceptions); DHS will provide notice to obligor, allow response/rebuttal, adjudicate, and, if administratively final, demand payment for the full bond amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing fees and forms required (Forms I-944, I-945, I-356, I-864 changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: New and revised information collection and forms: Form I-944 (Declaration of Self-Sufficiency) required for adjustment applicants, Form I-945 (Public Charge Bond), Form I-356 (Request for Cancellation), and elimination of Form I-864W.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which applications will require additional forms or evidence, associated new fees (added to 8 CFR 103.7), and DHS estimates of cost and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for extension of stay and change of status applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to 8 CFR 214.1 and 248.1: conditional approval of nonimmigrant extension/change of status based on demonstration that applicant has not received, is not receiving, and is not likely to receive public benefits as defined in 8 CFR 212.21(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where section 212(a)(4) applies, applicants must demonstrate non-receipt/likelihood standard; DHS may require a declaration of self-sufficiency (Form I-944) and will consider benefits received on or after the regulatory effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary requirements for adjustment of status (8 CFR 245.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustment of status applicants subject to public charge determination must submit a declaration of self-sufficiency on a DHS-designated form (Form I-944).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that Form I-944 is required to facilitate USCIS's public charge inadmissibility determination and enumerates evidentiary expectations tied to factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of a required affidavit of support as a factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The absence of a required affidavit of support may be considered in the public charge inadmissibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS discusses consequences when an affidavit of support is required but not provided and how it interacts with consideration of sponsorship and financial resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standards and USCIS evidentiary requirements (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may request evidence (RFE) and has specified evidentiary requirements for demonstrating factors relevant to public charge determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes potential RFEs for Forms I-944, credit reports, medical evidence (Form I-693), documentation of benefits receipt, and instructions that failing to provide requested evidence may affect the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with members of the armed forces and their families
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt of public benefits by active duty and reserve servicemembers and their families is considered under specified rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will not consider certain benefits received by enlisted members, active duty, Ready Reserve, or their spouses/children under specified statutory authorities; rule invites comments regarding such treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural instructions for public participation and comment submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All interested parties are invited to submit written comments; comments must reference DHS Docket No. USCIS-2010-0012, be in English (or include English translation), and will be posted to regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS requests comments that reference specific portions of the proposed rule, explain reasons for changes, and include supporting data/information/authority; warns that submissions will be posted without change and personal information will become public unless DHS determines withholding is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission methods and docket access
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies acceptable methods to submit comments (Federal eRulemaking Portal at regulations.gov preferred; mail address provided) and how to access the docket and background documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mailing address for Samantha Deshommes at USCIS, instructs to reference DHS Docket No. USCIS-2010-0012, and notes that mailed comments must be postmarked by the deadline; suggests signing up for email alerts on the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy notice and advice to commenters
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice that all submissions will be posted without change to the Federal eRulemaking Portal and will include any personal information provided; commenters may limit personal information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to the Privacy Act notice on regulations.gov footer; DHS may withhold information from public viewing if it impacts privacy or is offensive, at DHS's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic and cost/benefit considerations and familiarization costs
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS identifies expected burdens, costs, and benefits of the proposed rule (direct costs of forms, time burdens, reduction in transfer payments) and estimates familiarization time per person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides quantified estimates of annual and 10-year costs, sensitivity analyses for RFEs, potential reductions in federal/state transfer payments due to disenrollment, and an estimated 8-10 hour familiarization time per person for stakeholders.
